static_traits.name: Makayla
static_traits.family_status: Lives with a lizard named Nagini and a dog
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness;not yet received psychotherapy; self-criticism and Catastrophizing began during culinary school
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, organized thinking, able to give concrete examples; good cooperation but overall attitude rather negative, tending toward self-criticism and focusing on the negative, tone slightly Repressed.

basic_info.main_problem: I often catastrophize situations, for example deciding the whole meal is 'ruined' because one part is not perfect enough, thus producing feelings of inadequacy and self-criticism; Anxiety frequently occurs when Cooking for others or after receiving feedback, making it hard to enjoy others' praise.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent self-criticism and inability to fully appreciate cooking results affect mental health and love of cooking; hoping to reduce these negative thoughts and enjoy cooking more fully again.
growth_experiences: Catastrophizing and self-critical thought patterns began during culinary school training: often treating small mistakes as whole-dish failures, difficulty internalizing positive feedback; the coping approach then was actively seeking feedback and advice from mentors and peers. Recently intensified by pressure to impress others and make a good impression, gradually developing into difficulty enjoying praise, Sleep and appetite affected.

core_beliefs: I will never become a great Chef

special_situations.event: Prepared dinner for friends on the weekend; everyone liked it, but one appetizer was slightly overcooked
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a dish has a flaw, it means the whole meal fails, and I as a Chef am a failure too
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing attention on mistakes, negating others' praise, doubling self-criticism afterwards to force oneself to be more perfect next time
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I ruined this meal; I am not good enough

special_situations.event: When Cooking for others and Receiving compliments from others with positive feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot achieve perfection, I do not deserve praise
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating or reducing the weight of positive aspects, emphasizing inadequacy to maintain high standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are only praising me out of politeness; these strengths do not count

special_situations.event: After cooking, reviews the work and notices a small mistake
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A small mistake will foreshadow that I will always fail in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to 'prevent' future failure through excessive Reflection and self-blame, continuously pressuring oneself toward perfection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: One mistake means I will never become a great Chef

special_situations.event: Facing pressure at work to impress others (such as cooking for guests or friends)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Must satisfy everyone, otherwise it is failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Over-focusing on negative details, ignoring successes and positive feedback; constantly raising standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If someone is not satisfied, it proves I am not good enough

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and appreciated; to enjoy own achievements with peace of mind
core_conflict.fear: Fearing that imperfection will be negated and criticized, thus losing value and belonging
defense_goal: Avoiding being negated through harsh self-criticism and pursuing perfection
Focuses attention on flaws to maintain a sense of control

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough self needing perfection to gain recognition
object_relations.object_representation: A harsh judge (others not easily moved)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When praised or given positive feedback after cooking
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Viewing praise as untrue or out of politeness, believing small mistakes equal total failure (transference: others viewed as harsh judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a gentle, empathic tone, reflect their feelings, while inviting them to concretize and compare evidence: first affirm the effort, then pose open questions, avoid direct refutation; encourage them to state at least 3 positive facts and 1 point for improvement at the same time.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked to objectively review the strengths of a meal or discuss details of mistakes
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Separates emotions from events, talks rationally about technical details but finds it hard to experience joy and satisfaction
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Inviting them to do emotion naming and experiential exercises, tone steady and slow; using grounding and breathing Guidance, helping them pause after describing technical details to identify bodily sensations and emotion intensity.

manifestations: Unable to enjoy success and passion, praise hard to internalize; achievements swallowed by small mistakes, hard to experience satisfaction
outcomes: Declining enjoyment of cooking and increasing emptiness
Fluctuating sense of self-worth, hard to accept oneself

manifestations: Feeling bound by the expectation of 'must impress others and be perfect'
Treating external expectations as internal rules

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Self-talk carrying a 'must/should be perfect' tone
Internalizes others' expectations as one's own rigid standards

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Worrying that small mistakes will affect professional creativity, continuously pressuring oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not having discussed self-criticism troubles deeply with relatives and friends, instead directing critical energy at oneself
When receiving praise, not expressing acceptance outwardly, but inwardly intensifying self-pickiness

positive_force: Having solid cooking skills with works loved by others (friends praising flavors and plating)
Having the ability of self-observation and identifying cognitive biases (able to describe catastrophizing, black-and-white, etc.)
Has some social support (several relatives and friends to talk to)
Has coped by seeking feedback from mentors and peers, showing willingness to learn and adjust
Staying passionate about cooking with a clear desire to improve
negative_force: Significant cognitive biases: catastrophizing, black-and-white, mental filtering, negating the positive
Strong pressure of external evaluation and dependence on others' approval, difficulty internalizing self-worth
Persistent self-criticism and low sense of self-worth, prone to helplessness and Anxiety
Finds it hard to accept praise, affecting interpersonal interaction
Sleep and appetite affected by negative thinking, fluctuations in mood and energy

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizes small mistakes in cooking and criticizes herself harshly
antecedent: Receiving feedback or praise from others
Noticing flaws when reviewing the cooking process
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizing during culinary school the conditional worth of 'only perfection has value' and external validation tendency, worrying that imperfection means failure
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the risk of being negated, maintaining control and improving performance through pressure
target_behavior.consequence: Difficulty enjoying success, increased Anxiety and hopelessness, Sleep and appetite affected, worrying about damaged creativity

target_behavior.behavior: Negating and avoiding positive feedback (difficulty accepting others' praise)
antecedent: Others praise the dishes or give positive feedback
Being praised when sharing meals with family and friends
target_behavior.core_reason: Overly sensitive to external evaluation, believing imperfection does not deserve praise
target_behavior.function: Avoiding vulnerability and exposing flaws, maintaining Self-protection
target_behavior.consequence: Damaged Interpersonal relationships, reduced pleasure in shared meals, worsened inferiority and pressure
